questions: Do slalom line_loss_events fall from 0.3 toward 0 with the 12 mm footprint at the same positions?
Does the oval completion count hold at about 14 of 20 or better, with progress near 0.88?
Does either the s-bend or the slalom produce any completion, or any run that reaches progress above 0.5?
If slalom line loss does not fall, is the outer span (x = ±0.06 m) the limit? Would you want a wider span at x = ±0.07 m next?
Does max_error on the failing runs stay at about 0.064 m, or does it show a sharp-bend pattern at the same place each run?

intent: Keep the iteration 7 platform that completed 14 of 20 oval runs (0.6 kg, 0.12 m body, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels, seven sensors at y = 0.02 m with x = ±0.06 m). Change only the sensor footprint from 16 mm to 12 mm, to cut slalom line loss (0.3 events per run) without disturbing yaw inertia or speed.
learning: Iteration 7 shows that the 0.6 kg, y = 0.02 m, 16 mm design completes the oval in 70 percent of trials, while the s-bend and slalom still end off track. Footprint is the next sensing variable to test on the slalom, because it is the only geometry lever that has not been changed at this inertia. If 12 mm lowers slalom line loss but completions do not appear on the s-bend or slalom, the remaining limit is turn authority (wheel_track), which the Integrator should treat as the next geometry question.
rationale: Iteration 7 (0.6 kg, 0.12 m body, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels, seven 16 mm sensors at y = 0.02 m, x = ±0.06 m) is the best design so far at 303.8. On the oval it finished 14 of 20 runs (progress 0.88, mean finish 1.63 s), so the oval is now a completion. The s-bend and slalom still end 20 of 20 off track, at progress 0.27 and 0.12. Slalom line loss is 0.3 events per run, up from zero at 0.8 kg in iteration 5. The Integrator's stated trigger for a footprint change (slalom line loss above about 0.25 at 0.6 kg, y = 0.02 m) has been met. Max_error on the oval finishes is 0.048, so the robot can hold the line when it is not in a sharp bend. The failures on the s-bend and slalom look like sharp-bend losses, not a general tracking floor. Iteration 6 showed that a larger wheel radius cuts progress, so speed is not the lever. I will keep every value that produced the oval completions and change only the sensor footprint, from 16 mm to 12 mm, at the same positions. The Integrator asked for this test, and it isolates the sensing cause of the slalom line loss without touching yaw inertia, track or reaction point. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0, oval completions hold at about 14 of 20 or better, and the score stays near or above 300. A completion on the s-bend or slalom would add about 500 points per run, so those tracks are the next target if the oval holds. If line loss does not fall with 12 mm, the next geometry test is a wider outer span (x = ±0.07 m) to give the line more margin before the robot leaves the track.
